new_statements.relation_note: Stress non-phonemic in all languages of the survey; default stress = first non-schwa syllable (marking convention); nothing on tone; (e) field gives only gender-class and affix-order typology (2CA, SpOs) for Beli, and a phylum-wide consonant/vowel note elsewhere.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Survey-level, first-hand (Laycock's own 1967 field transcriptions): stress is not phonemic in any of the Lumi Subdistrict languages, Beli included; in the wordlists stress is left unmarked when it falls on the first syllable whose vowel is not schwa, i.e. the default/predictable position is the leftmost full-vowel syllable (word-initial unless the initial syllable has ə), and only deviations are marked. In the published Beli list (44 items, via TransNewGuinea/Rosetta) exactly one form carries a mark, nehé 'earth', so the remaining forms (e.g. fasən, masən, pəriyen, səkwoho, waluko, kalkopo) are by that convention stressed on their first non-schwa syllable.
new_statements.exceptions: Marked exceptions only: in the Beli list nehé 'earth/ground' (final stress) is the single accented form.
new_statements.identity_note: The article's language list has an explicit entry 'Beli (Akuwagel, Mukili)' with villages Aimukili, Makafim, Makafu, Mukili, Waniwomaka, Yemeraba, Yulam (Maimai-Namblo CD), informant Sulu (Makafim), recorded Nuku 7/67 = Laycock 1973 entry 39 BELI [bey] (test list DCL67 Sulu/Makafim). The stress sentence is an article-wide statement about all languages surveyed in the Lumi Subdistrict report ('any of these languages'), Beli being one of them; it is not a Beli-specific paragraph.
